rule: A lexicon siglum that ROMAN_RE reads as a roman numeral is dropped as a volume marker UNLESS the VisualDCS counting workbook lists it as a catalogue key in its Details column. The exemption is this committed allowlist, never a rule inferred at run time, so an offline run without the workbook behaves identically.
rejected_alternatives: Keep roman sigla that lead a witness string: discriminates nothing, all 67 dropped sigla lead, because II/III are orphaned volume markers whose catalogue was stripped upstream ('Hpr. III. 49' split into two witnesses, leaving 'II. 48').
Keep roman sigla that rarely follow another catalogue: II reads 53-after/132-standalone, MD reads 12-after/17-standalone, so MD scores WORSE than II.

source.workbook_total_never_a_census: 1,032,077 is the sum of the mss column over 140,848 rows of the workbook; it is never quoted as a manuscript census.

entries.evidence: MD. 4397 / MD. 6571-74 / MD. 8771 / MD. 4695 are accession runs, exactly like other catalogues; 11,672 witnesses in the shipped mss_witnesses field, always at position 0 of the witness string (a volume marker cannot lead a witness field, and II/III only ever appear orphaned); the workbook's Details vocabulary lists 'MD.: n { ... }'; no NCC volume runs to 1,500.
entries.defect_it_closes: MD. never terminated a segment, so MD accessions folded into the catalogue before them: 2 of the 12 false positives in the H7080 seed-20261018 draw (Adyar 6571, Jain 8771), 1.92 % of pilot units (14/730), and 0 of 100 sampled rows carrying siglum MD.
